summary: Radar for 5 Oct 2026. Most of the news is still coming out of EASD/EADV week. Next-generation drugs and the muscle question are the strongest themes. The best early opportunities: (1) the survodutide NEJM paper (SYNCHRONIZE-2: 13.1% vs 3.1% at 76 weeks in adults with obesity and T2D), with Bloomberg and Fierce calling it a "disappointment". That makes a ready-made headline decoder with a named drug. (2) Regeneron's trevogrumab plus semaglutide (COURAGE Phase 2: lean mass −4.2% vs −7.3% at 52 weeks, with total weight loss about the same). It ties straight into our muscle pillar. (3) A UK study in Anaesthesia of 47,039 patients: regurgitation or aspiration under anaesthesia was 1.41% in GLP-1 users vs 0.12% in non-users. The useful message is "tell your surgical team"; it is not stopping advice. (4) Petrelintide's full paper in Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology, which feeds the "amylin is next" story. Retatrutide TRIUMPH-2 is now peer-reviewed in The Lancet (23.4% in the BMI 35+ subgroup on the highest dose) and is moving from rising to peaking. Only worth it with a "what peer review added" angle that keeps the not-approved hedge and the warning about online sellers. Nail detachment ("Ozempic nails", EADV survey) and hair loss in men (NYU genetic study, now in the Washington Post) are rising in mainstream news. We already made a nails Short (S2 10-01, held for a scope error), so that topic should go to long-form or carousel with the controls-only scope written correctly. Seasonal hook: Medicare Open Enrollment starts 15 Oct, and the $50 Medicare GLP-1 Bridge (Wegovy, Foundayo, Zepbound KwikPen, through 2027) is what our 55–65 viewers will be searching for. The WashU stopping study and the SELECT mediation analysis are fading and are not repeated here. GLP-1 microdosing lifestyle content keeps turning up in Yahoo Creators syndication and is marked reject.

candidates.topic: Survodutide in obesity + type 2 diabetes (SYNCHRONIZE-2, NEJM 1 Oct 2026): up to 13.1% vs 3.1% placebo weight loss at 76 weeks, and why markets called it a 'disappointment'
candidates.angle: Headline decoder: 'Survodutide lost 13% and still disappointed. Why?' Explain the glucagon + GLP-1 dual mechanism (liver-fat angle), how people with T2D typically lose less on every drug, and compare honestly against published trials (no head-to-head). GI side effects: 72.8–77.7% vs 38.6% placebo, mostly mild to moderate. Investigational, not approved as of Oct 2026.
candidates.predicted_peak: 5–14 days (as approval-timeline coverage and creators catch up)
candidates.why_now: NEJM paper plus Bloomberg, Fierce and BioSpace 'disappointment' framing on 1–2 Oct. A STAT Pharmalittle mention and an Oct 1 Contemp Clin Trials review also appear in today's signals. Our verification found almost no creator explainers yet. Named-drug headline decoder = our best title formula.

evidence.signal: SYNCHRONIZE-2 full paper, n=752, adults with obesity and T2D, 76 weeks
Up to 13.1% vs 3.1% placebo; A1C down up to 1.21%
'Boehringer, Zealand obesity drug's 13% weight loss disappoints'
Zealand stock slides as drug 'underwhelms again' in Phase 3

candidates.topic: Trevogrumab + semaglutide (Regeneron COURAGE Phase 2): lean mass loss −4.2% vs −7.3% with semaglutide alone at 52 weeks (about 42% less), with no meaningful extra weight loss
candidates.angle: 'Can a drug protect muscle on semaglutide (Wegovy)?' Myostatin explained simply. What COURAGE showed and what it didn't: company-funded Phase 2, investigational, no approval, no evidence it improves strength or outcomes yet. Then pivot to what's proven today: protein (with the kidney caveat) and strength training.
candidates.why_now: Regeneron release on 1 Oct, then Medical Daily, Medical Dialogues and Inc. ('could make Wegovy even more effective') on 3–5 Oct. 'Ozempic muscle loss' is a big evergreen search and Yahoo published a 'muscle loss is real' piece today. Few creator videos on trevogrumab specifically.

evidence.signal: Phase 2 COURAGE: lean mass preserved during GLP-1-induced weight loss
About 42% less lean mass lost at the 75 mg dose over one year
Anti-myostatin preserved lean mass during and after semaglutide weight loss

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines and anaesthesia: regurgitation or aspiration in 1.41% of GLP-1 users vs 0.12% of non-users (UK prospective cohort, 47,039 patients, 119 sites, Anaesthesia)
candidates.angle: 'On semaglutide or tirzepatide and having surgery? The one thing to tell your anaesthetist.' Explain slower stomach emptying (a core mechanism), what the study found (19 events among 1,348 GLP-1 users, mostly during waking from anaesthesia, observational), and why guidance differs between societies. The action is 'tell your surgical team and follow their instructions'. Never tell viewers to stop or pause on their own.
candidates.why_now: Healthday/MedicalXpress picked it up on 2 Oct (presented at the Anesthesiology annual meeting). Medscape has 'Why can't societies agree?'. People constantly search whether to stop before surgery, so a correct and safe explainer adds value. Moderate creator coverage, mostly older 2023–24 pieces.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 linked to 11-fold higher regurgitation rate under anaesthesia
1.41% vs 0.12%; 17 regurgitations + 2 aspirations; variable perioperative management
Society guidance on GLP-1s before surgery still conflicts

candidates.topic: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge: $50/month for Wegovy (injection and pill), Foundayo (orforglipron) and the Zepbound KwikPen through Dec 2027, just as Medicare Open Enrollment opens on 15 Oct
candidates.angle: 'Medicare and Wegovy/Zepbound in 2026: what the $50 Bridge covers.' Plain-English explainer for people 65+: which products are included (and that Zepbound vials and single-dose pens are not), that the $50 doesn't count toward the Part D out-of-pocket cap, and to check eligibility with your plan and prescriber. Medicaid and Rhode Island coverage changes go in as context. No pricing hype; cite medicare.gov.
candidates.why_now: ABC7 covered the Bridge on 4 Oct. Rhode Island Medicaid has ended weight-loss-only coverage. Open Enrollment (15 Oct) is a predictable seasonal search spike for our 55–65+ viewers. Competition is mostly insurance-broker blogs, not trusted health explainers.

evidence.signal: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge: GLP-1 drugs for $50 a month
Bridge runs from July through end of 2027; covered products listed
Eligibility, costs and coverage explained

candidates.topic: Petrelintide (amylin analogue, ZUPREME-1, Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology): 8.7–10.7% vs 1.7% placebo weight loss at 42 weeks; nausea 20% vs 6%
candidates.angle: 'What is amylin, and why are Lilly and Novo betting on it after GLP-1?' A mechanism explainer for the second fullness hormone, positioned next to CagriSema and EloraTZP (amylin + GLP-1 combos). Petrelintide alone loses less than tirzepatide but may be gentler. Investigational, now in Phase 3.
keywords: next weight loss drug after Ozempic
candidates.why_now: Lancet D&E paper on 29 Sep plus the CNBC feature on 2 Oct ('Why Lilly and Novo are betting on amylin'). A Diabetes Ther review on amylin agonists also appears in today's signals, and the snapshots show EloraTZP at momentum ~90. Search phrasing ('amylin') hasn't peaked yet.

evidence.signal: ZUPREME-1 Phase 2, n=485, 42 weeks
About 10% weight loss, nausea in 20%, moving into Phase 3
Why Lilly and Novo are betting on amylin

candidates.topic: Retatrutide TRIUMPH-2 now peer-reviewed in The Lancet: 23.4% average weight loss on the highest dose in adults with T2D and BMI 35+ at 80 weeks; adverse-event discontinuation 12.1% vs 4.8% placebo
candidates.angle: 'Retatrutide is peer-reviewed. What changed from the headlines?' Decode the NDTV '25%' claim versus the actual subgroup figures, include the discontinuation numbers, state it is not approved as of Oct 2026, and repeat Lilly's warning that 'research' retatrutide sold online isn't its trial drug. Never point to any source.
candidates.why_now: Lancet paper on 29 Sep, then MedPage, Clinical Trials Arena, NDTV and a 'GLP-3' explainer on 2–4 Oct. Search autocomplete is full of 'retatrutide approval status'. High coverage, but our attributed-correction Short on retatrutide outperformed, so a differentiated angle is still worth it.

evidence.signal: TRIUMPH-2 results, T2D + obesity/overweight
Peer-reviewed: 23.4% (60.8 lb) at the highest dose in BMI 35+ subgroup; discontinuation 8.8–12.1% vs 4.8%
TRIUMPH-2 Phase 3 publication

candidates.topic: 'Ozempic nails': nail detachment reported by 39.3% of GLP-1 users vs 8.7% of controls with T2D and/or obesity (EADV 2026 cross-sectional survey, 575 users vs 1,329 controls)
candidates.angle: 'Are semaglutide (Ozempic) and tirzepatide making nails lift?' Self-reported, cross-sectional data, can't prove cause, and about half of users had nail problems before treatment. Likely link: rapid weight loss and low protein intake. Practical, protein-forward habits with the kidney caveat, and when to see a dermatologist. Scope rule: only the controls are described as having T2D and/or obesity.
candidates.why_now: NewsNation, Medical Daily, Gizmodo and Inc. covered it on 2–4 Oct, and an 'Ozempic nail' explainer term is forming. We already ran a Short on 10-01 (held for the controls-scope error), so this should go to long-form or carousel with corrected scope plus a hair-and-nails tie-in.

evidence.signal: Nail detachment about 4 times more common with GLP-1 use
GLP-1 users report more nail detachment and hair loss than non-users
'Hair loss was just the start. Ozempic users also reporting nail trouble'

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and hair loss in men: NYU genetic (Mendelian randomisation) study links higher GLP-1 receptor activity to about 7% added risk of pattern hair loss in genetically predisposed men
candidates.angle: 'Ozempic hair loss in men: is it genetic?' What Mendelian randomisation can and can't tell us (genetic proxies, not people taking the drug), how it fits with the BMJ cohort data, why rapid weight loss alone can trigger shedding (telogen effluvium), and what to ask a clinician.
candidates.why_now: Washington Post (3 Oct) and ABC30 brought the September J Invest Dermatol study to mainstream audiences, and hair loss is already on our double-down list. Lots of generic hair-loss videos exist, but few cover the male genetic angle accurately.

evidence.signal: Some hair loss in men linked to use of weight-loss drugs (Mendelian randomisation, 205,327 people)
GLP-1 drugs could nudge some men toward hair loss
New study suggests possible connection between GLP-1s and hair loss in men

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound) body composition in real-world use: fat mass −35.4%, fat-free mass −5.1%, skeletal muscle mass stable at 24 weeks (J Diabetes Complications)
candidates.angle: 'Does tirzepatide (Mounjaro) burn fat or muscle?' A search-style mechanism question. Real-world, single-arm, short-term data, set against the SURMOUNT DXA substudy. Fat-free mass includes water and organs, which is not the same as muscle. Protein and strength training still matter (protein caveat for kidney disease).
candidates.why_now: News-Medical write-up on 2 Oct ('preserving skeletal muscle') is already being shared with an overstated framing. An Obesity Pillars pilot on exercise plus nutrition and an aesthetic-surgery lean-mass review also appear in today's signals. Our 'Does Mounjaro speed up metabolism?' Short was the #2 performer.

evidence.signal: Fat mass −35.4%, fat-free mass −5.1% over 24 weeks
Effects of tirzepatide on body weight and composition in adults with overweight and obesity
Fat and lean mass with incretin therapy plus structured exercise and nutrition

candidates.topic: Semaglutide (Wegovy) and liver fat: 23 of 26 adults with obesity reached normal liver fat by week 72 (STEP UP MRI subset, post hoc, no placebo comparison reported)
candidates.angle: 'Can semaglutide (Wegovy) clear fatty liver?' Bring in MASH, cite the stronger ESSENCE trial evidence first, then present the STEP UP figure honestly: small, exploratory, within-group, Novo-reported. Fits the benefits-beyond-weight pillar with a named drug.
candidates.why_now: Novo's EASD release on 2–3 Oct got Benzinga and Medical Daily coverage. Fatty liver is a large evergreen search with few accurate GLP-1-specific explainers.

evidence.signal: Liver fat fell to normal in 23 of 26 in a small post hoc analysis
Exploratory STEP UP analysis, mean liver fat 8.8% to 3.1%

candidates.topic: How semaglutide may protect kidneys in type 2 diabetes: Nature Medicine mechanistic RCT (biopsy + MRI, n=33). The coprimary MRI outcomes were not significantly different from placebo, but secondary signals pointed to less fibrosis progression and lower vascular resistance
candidates.angle: 'Why does semaglutide (Ozempic) help kidneys?' Lead with FLOW (24% lower risk of major kidney events in adults with T2D and CKD), then this new trial's 'how' clues. Report the null coprimary results exactly, and note it was small and the findings came from secondary outcomes.
candidates.why_now: Nature Medicine on 1 Oct, plus several GLP-1 + SGLT2 kidney papers this week (Diabetes Obes Metab, Intern Med J). Low creator coverage. Repackages a benefit topic with a named drug and comparator, per the playbook.

evidence.signal: Effects of semaglutide on kidney disease in type 2 diabetes: randomized placebo-controlled trial
FLOW: semaglutide reduced major kidney disease events by 24%

candidates.topic: Oral GLP-1 race: Foundayo (orforglipron) prescriptions surging vs the Wegovy pill (Fierce Oral GLP-1 Tracker), plus ACHIEVE-4 cardiovascular safety (MACE-4 HR 0.84 vs insulin glargine, non-inferior)
candidates.angle: 'Foundayo vs the Wegovy pill: how they differ.' Food and timing rules as labelled (no dosing), the trial results each pill has, CV safety data in T2D, and why 'surging' is a sales story, not an efficacy verdict. Use absolute event rates for ACHIEVE-4 and avoid repeating the S3 10-01 angle.
candidates.why_now: Fierce tracker on 2 Oct, a Yahoo 'pill vs shot' doctor piece, and lots of 'is the Wegovy pill effective' search-phrase pages. ACHIEVE-4 is in The Lancet. Pills are our search-proven pillar.

evidence.signal: Lilly's Foundayo surges as Novo's Wegovy pill stalls
Foundayo demonstrated cardiovascular safety in ACHIEVE-4
ACHIEVE-4: MACE-4 HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.59–1.20), non-inferior

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) and diabetic eye disease: linked to lower diabetic retinopathy risk in a 174,000-patient US cohort, with no increase in retinopathy vs dulaglutide in the SURPASS-CVOT retina substudy
candidates.angle: 'Does Mounjaro affect your eyes?' A calm explainer: the observational cohort only shows an association (0.49% vs 0.57% mild retinopathy at 12 months vs lifestyle alone), the randomised substudy showed no worsening vs dulaglutide over 36 months, and why rapid A1C drops warrant eye checks. Can link to the semaglutide NAION topic from earlier snapshots.
candidates.why_now: Medical Economics flagged it again on 3 Oct, and eye safety stays a constant worry after the NAION headlines. Few tirzepatide-specific eye explainers.

evidence.signal: Tirzepatide and reduced risk of diabetic retinopathy: multicenter US cohort
No increased retinopathy risk with tirzepatide (SURPASS-CVOT retina substudy)

candidates.topic: Hydration on semaglutide or tirzepatide in hot weather: reduced thirst, nausea/vomiting and dehydration-related kidney risk (doctor warnings during the latest heat wave)
candidates.angle: 'Why you might forget to drink on Ozempic or Mounjaro.' The appetite and thirst mechanism, warning signs (dark urine, dizziness), and simple habits like phone reminders and water-rich foods, always with 'unless you've been told to limit fluids'. Red flag: severe vomiting or no urination means contact a clinician. Works for an Australian spring/summer audience too.
candidates.why_now: ABC News GMA piece on 3 Oct during a heat wave. Hydration is a core 'getting the most from GLP-1' pillar, and it's a searchable side-effect habit.

evidence.signal: Amid heat wave, doctors warn of health risks for people taking GLP-1 drugs
Heat-related health risks higher for people taking GLP-1s

candidates.topic: GLP-1 use after childbirth up about 24-fold (0.08% to 1.9%, 2018–2025, privately insured US mothers, JAMA), while breastfeeding safety data remain limited; new French nationwide pregnancy-safety study in Diabetologia
candidates.angle: 'GLP-1s after pregnancy: what we know and don't.' A balanced explainer covering why use is rising, what labels say about pregnancy and breastfeeding (talk to your obstetrician/prescriber), and what the French registry adds. No advice to start or stop.
candidates.why_now: U.S. News, Yahoo, Medical Daily and Bioengineer were still running it on 2–4 Oct, and it has now appeared in 3 snapshots. The Diabetologia pregnancy study is a fresh hook.

evidence.signal: Postpartum GLP-1 prescriptions rose nearly 24-fold; breastfeeding data limited
Safety of GLP-1 RAs in type 2 diabetes pregnancy: French nationwide study

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines and inflammatory skin disease: nationwide cohort in hidradenitis suppurativa (JEADV) and a psoriasis review (Clin Dermatol)
candidates.angle: 'Could semaglutide help inflammatory skin conditions?' An early-research explainer in the 'promising, not proven' framing: observational and review evidence only, and not an approved use.
candidates.why_now: Two new dermatology papers (1 and 3 Oct) during EADV week. Very little creator coverage, but search demand is also small, so this fits a carousel or a slot in a 'beyond weight' long-form.

evidence.source: PubMed / J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol
evidence.signal: GLP-1 RAs in hidradenitis suppurativa: nationwide cohort study
GLP-1 receptor agonists in psoriasis management

candidates.topic: 'GLP-1 microdosing' lifestyle content (Yahoo Creators syndication: 'Microdosing GLP-1s like Ozempic is everywhere')
candidates.angle: Do not produce. Microdosing and self-titration protocols are on the never-cover list and usually lead to gray-market sources. If any later piece needs to address it, the only allowed line is that no approved dosing schedule exists outside the label and dosing is a decision for your prescriber.
candidates.why_now: Keeps reappearing (Yahoo Creators 2 Oct; MindBodyGreen in an earlier snapshot). Flagged so downstream agents don't pick it up.

evidence.signal: 'Microdosing GLP-1s like Ozempic is everywhere'
